objectClass.notes: Lashed bamboo, nothing hinged and nothing attaching: one root pivot, zero sockets. A riverside sala or beach-mat table sat at from the floor, placed in twos and threes, so the two draw calls are the design constraint. Riversides, beach mats, rural salas; honey-tan slats with grain and a knot, grey-blue culm rails flaking to pale patches and wound with cream twine, tan legs and stretchers lashed at every joint, sat at from the floor.

reasoning: TWO components on TWO materials: the TIMBER top (seven slat boxes, two hidden battens, four legs, four stretchers, eight joint twine bands, the knot, the tag and bow merged) and the CULM rails (two open rails, four rim-and-bore lathe pairs, sixteen twine turns and two ties merged). Two draw calls of two.

Two materials because the honey sawn slats and tan poles (0.72, a sawn-grain canvas) and the weathered grey-blue culm rails (0.60, a culm canvas with node rings) share neither tone nor texture; both WHITE with the tones as vertex colours.
No repetition system: seven slats are seven boxes inside the top merge.
Action readiness: one root pivot, zero sockets, one declared box collider, not breakable.

specDepthDecision.rationale: The identity is seven THICK slats with visible gaps between two fat grey culm RAILS wound with twine, their cut ends hollow, on tan legs with a lashed stretcher overrunning them. Twenty thin battens, or grey posts standing through the top, would be a different table; the gaps, the wound rails and the hollow ends are what the plate shows.

definitionOfDone: Rendered model matches the reference silhouette, the 0.57 x 0.42 x 0.47 m proportions, the visible component hierarchy and the material response for a real-time browser prop.
All four scene-budget ceilings hold: <=2000 triangles, <=2 draw calls, <=2 materials, <=4 unique geometries.
Zero coincident co-facing surface pairs (check-coplanar clean).
Exactly one root pivot plus 0 named mechanism pivot(s); zero sockets; box collider; no destruction groups.
Every material declares textureless with named evidence.

silhouette.description: Two r 0.033 culm rails along z at x +-0.252, crowns at 0.42, 0.47 long with hollow ends; seven 0.054 x 0.040 x 0.40 slats at 0.061 pitch topping at 0.41 between them on two hidden battens; four r 0.027 tan legs on +-0.252 x +-0.17 to the rail undersides; r 0.021 stretchers at 0.12 (x, overrunning the legs 0.06) and 0.15 (z); eight twine turns per rail, twine bands at every leg joint.
silhouette.envelopeDerivation: x +-0.285 at the rail skins (0.57), y 0 to 0.420 at the rail crowns, z +-0.235 at the rail ends (0.47); the front and back stretchers overrun the legs to x +-0.312. The LIST-TIME declaration was 0.90 x 0.42 x 0.60 (w/h 2.14, d/h 1.43). The Meshy proxy of the plate measures bbox 1.889 x 1.399 x 1.555, w/h 1.351 and d/h 1.112. The plate is a steep top-down view that hides the height, and the declared 0.42 is the identity (a LOW table), so height is kept and the plan follows the proxy: 0.42 x 1.351 = 0.567 -> 0.57 m by 0.42 x 1.112 = 0.467 -> 0.47 m; the declaration was corrected before building. The materials agree: on a 0.57 m top the plate's slats (74 px pitch of a 750 px width) are 0.056 m and its 60 px posts 0.046 m -- split bamboo and a culm -- where at 0.90 m they would be 0.09 and 0.07. Stations off the proxy (occupancy, 50 rows of H, 80 columns of W): full-height edge columns 5-13 and 66-74 (centres +-0.433 W = +-0.245) from row 0.00 to 0.98 -- the LEGS under the rail ends topped by the RAILS, which the first build read as posts proud of the top; slat top faces at row 0.94 with slat SIDE faces as seven vertical columns over rows 0.86-0.92 (0.040 m thick -- few and thick); a stretcher ring at rows 0.20-0.30; leg z range 0.90 D, so leg centres at z +-0.17. SECOND BUILD (2026-09-02) re-read the plate at zoom (z-rail.png, z-legs.png): the two grey weathered culms are HORIZONTAL side rails lying along the slat ends at the top, each wound with eight spaced twine turns and tied at its far end, its cut end hollow; under each rail end a tan bamboo leg; the front stretcher is lashed to the legs and overruns them ~6 cm; the slats lie between the rails.
silhouette.meshyCrossCheck: Independent Meshy v7 reconstruction of the same plate: bbox 1.889 x 1.399 x 1.555, w/h 1.351 and d/h 1.112, which corrected the declared 0.90 x 0.60 plan to 0.57 x 0.47. Its slat pitch reads 0.074 because the 20 mm voxel fuses each slat with its gap; the plate's 74 px of 750 (0.056-0.061) is used instead. Its full-height edge columns are legs under rails, not posts -- the proxy cannot separate the two, and the plate at zoom can.

viewEvidence.note: The grey culm: a horizontal side RAIL, wound with twine, hollow at its cut end (z-rail.png).
NOT OBSERVED. The plate looks down on the top; the rails, the stretcher ring height and the post length are the proxy's (rows 0.78-0.84 and 0.20-0.30), confidence 0.7.

evidence: Measured on the plate: slats #eec093 / #e9b179 (187-201) with a shaded slat at #bea288 (167) and a knot; analyze_texture meanLum 175 sat 0.45 mottle 0.10; extract_pbr_evidence palette #E8B98C #E0A974 #F2CAA0 #6E3F1E #B38157 at confidence 0.835.

Textureless as DECLARED: slats 0xd69c5e (warmed from 0xd9a86e, which probed 202-205 and read pale-yellow against the plate's honey 187-201) and poles 0xc4945e as vertex colours under a 512 px sawn-grain canvas at 0.30 m through world UVs with 420 grain lines and seven splits (the plate's slats carry strong dark grain and cracks); the knot a darker disc 0.5 mm proud.
textureless.note: Declared textureless so createSculptMaterial skips makeProceduralTextureSet entirely -- FIVE canvases per material written pixel by pixel, at a cost that is the SQUARE of the resolution. It is also a correctness fix: with a texture set the generator forces color to white and roughness to 1 and reads both from the generated maps, discarding this measured albedo.

lodPlan.strategy: full component tree and material layers
merge static components and reduce local feature geometry

performanceBudget.optimizationPolicy: Real-time browser FPS prop on low-end integrated GPUs; a level builder places hundreds at once. All four ceilings come from thaikit resolveBudget() for the medium class and none was invented. The component split was costed against the DRAW-CALL ceiling in the blockout, before any geometry existed: parts that share a material are merged into one component rather than left to be merged later, because a pivot hung off a part cannot be merged afterwards.

materials.note: timber and culm: 2 of 2; every tone within each is a vertex colour.

uniqueGeometries.note: One per component plus one per repetition system. A scaled box is NOT a shared geometry -- the generator bakes real dimensions in via geometry.scale(), so every differently-sized box is genuinely distinct. Each InstancedMesh reuses a single geometry across all its instances, which is the whole point.

triangles.note: 1688 of 2000: fourteen boxes, sixteen 10-segment cylinders, two open 12-segment rails, eight 12-segment lathes, sixteen open 10-segment twine bands and an 8-segment disc.

lightingFromPhoto.notes: The plate is a flat studio lightbox: surfaces at 90 degrees to each other measure within a few levels, which is only possible under near-shadowless illumination. That is WHY the measured crop means are usable as albedo with little correction.
High fill ratio inferred from the shadow-side wall retaining full value.

The seamless backdrop acts as a large uniform environment. The thaikit harness supplies NO environment map, which is why every metal on this prop carries a metalness well below its physical value -- a metal with nothing to reflect renders black.
NO rim light in the plate. Recorded so a missing rim in the render is not read as a defect.
Exposure 1.0 with ACES filmic tone mapping; no exposure compensation is applied to the measured albedos and none is warranted.

NO contact or ground shadow in the plate -- it is a cut-out against a seamless backdrop. Recorded so the absence is not read as a missing feature. IN USE this is a floor-placed building and the HOST scene owns its contact shadow: castShadow ships enabled on every mesh and the factory defines no ground plane of its own.

proceduralStrategy.strategy: Boxes for the slats, battens, tag and ties; cylinders for legs, stretchers, rails and twine; lathes for the rails' cut ends.
No InstancedMesh at two draw calls. In a scene the HOST instances the table.
All procedural variation is assigned by instance INDEX, never from a random source, so the model is byte-identical on every build.
Both materials are declared textureless. Two 512 px canvases after construction -- sawn grain on the timber, culm rings and streaks on the culm -- 2 MB; the factory built in under 100 ms.
